violated_invariant: Collateral valuation must not be movable within a transaction by an unprivileged donation; the oracle for wrapped xStock collateral tracked an ERC4626 convertToAssets() rate that a direct underlying transfer inflates.
notes: AaveOracle (0xbd49) is unmodified Aave v3 code; getAssetPrice simply returns latestAnswer() from the configured per-asset source. The actual manipulable logic sits in the wGOOGLx price adapter / ERC4626 wrapper (0x1630, unverified, not a candidate), so the defect in recovered source is the trust placed in that source. None of the Slither findings describe a manipulable price source; calls-loop and missing-zero-check are true but harmless.

violated_invariant: Vault share price must not be inflatable by a same-transaction donation; FleetCommander NAV is the live, unguarded sum of each Ark's totalAssets(), including an Ark being offboarded whose Silo vgUSDC position was counted at par.
notes: FleetCommander deployed at block 21795049, before the fork, so the recovered source is pre-patch. NAV is computed by looping _arks[i].totalAssets() with no donation or deviation guard (the NatSpec itself says it relies on accurate Ark reporting); public analyses add that the donated-into Ark had been capped to zero for offboarding but was still in the active set. The calls-loop findings on _sumTotalAssets touch the defect line but describe gas/DoS risk, not the inflatable valuation, so they do not explain the exploit.

violated_invariant: A single actor should not be able to buy a quorum of votes on the open market, pass a proposal that hands over the ProxyAdmin, and upgrade a fund-holding proxy; a 200k-vote quorum against instantly-minable STRNGR votes made this cheap.
notes: The catalog victims are both AdminUpgradeabilityProxy forwarders; the Governor implementation (0xf6c7...) and StrongPoolV5 implementation (0xe89c...) that hold the quorum and mineForVotesOnly logic were not recovered, so no defect location can be named from source. Kept in scope as governance_design rather than designed behavior because the taxonomy explicitly covers governance capture, but the contracts did execute their rules as written. The incorrect-return / incorrect-modifier findings on the proxies are the usual false positives on the ifAdmin fallback pattern.

violated_invariant: The factory must only ever issue the intended initializePool/mint calls to the PositionManager on behalf of itself; forwarding caller-supplied bytes verbatim let anyone make the factory call setApprovalForAll on every LP NFT it custodies.
notes: launch() is permissionless and passes initCalldata and modifyCalldata straight into IPositionManager.multicall with no selector or target validation, which is exactly the forwarded call the PoC abuses. Slither has no finding for this: arbitrary-send-eth (index 0) is about the dust refund to msg.sender, which is intended, so it is marked invalid; the unchecked-transfer and unused-return hits on launch are real but cosmetic.

violated_invariant: Redeeming X FUM in one defund() should pay at least as much ETH as redeeming X FUM across many consecutive defund() calls; the averaged sliding-price approximation plus per-call adjShrinkFactor contraction is not split-invariant.
notes: ethFromDefund prices a burn off the arithmetic mean of the starting and an estimated ending FUM sell price, and each call shrinks bidAskAdjustment, so slicing one redemption into 64 pieces pays more ETH than the lump sum; no oracle input moves. The divide-before-multiply findings sit in checkForFreshOraclePrice and _storeState, not in the redemption curve, and do not describe the flaw. The reentrancy-no-eth on _defundFum is marked invalid because the only pre-state-write external call is to the protocol's own FUM token.

violated_invariant: Share mint/burn valuation must not depend on the instantaneous Uniswap V3 slot0 price; the vault's TWAP/deviation guard covered only the manager rebalance path, so a swap-skewed tick let a caller mint and burn at a favourable token mix.
notes: The only victim candidate is the EIP173Proxy; the ArrakisVaultV1 implementation (0xd68b...) that holds mint/burn/getUnderlyingBalances was not recovered, so the location names come from the PoC and public G-UNI source, not from a recovered candidate. The proxy's controlled-delegatecall finding is the owner-gated init-call pattern and is not the exploited weakness.

violated_invariant: Voting power over a vault should track a meaningful share of the vault's economic ownership; because only ~0.05 gtmvETH of wrapped shares existed, one depositor who wrapped a single share held a supermajority and could pass a proposal that rerouted the vault's debt to an attacker strategy.
notes: None of the six candidates (Yearn V3 meta-vault, Aragon TokenVoting, DAO, Zodiac modifiers, wrapped governance token) has recovered source, so no code location or Slither adjudication is possible. The PoC reconstructs a legitimate proposal/vote/execute flow rather than a key compromise, so it is kept in scope under governance_design with the same designed-behavior caveat as StrongBlock.

violated_invariant: Only the current manager may change the delegate implementations that item-adapter clones delegatecall into; an unprotected, re-runnable initialize() let any caller become manager and register code that transfers items without owner approval.
notes: The catalog carries no victim address; the two contract registries hijacked via initialize()/acceptManager() and the ERC-1155 platform are unverified, so the only recovered candidate is the ENJToken, which is merely the drained asset. Root cause follows the PoC's trace description of a re-runnable initializer that reassigns the manager; it could not be checked against source.

violated_invariant: A liquidation must not let a party controlling both the borrower and the taker extract more collateral value than the quote it repays; Ajna's oracle-free auction/bucket pricing and the bucketTake/take/repayDebt accounting let the attacker's self-liquidation shift the loss onto other lenders.
notes: The pool proxy 0xad24 is unverified and the ERC20Pool implementation (0x05bb...) is not a candidate, so no Slither findings exist on the victim; the only sourced candidate is the cbETH FiatTokenProxy, which is the collateral token. Press coverage agrees it was internal liquidation accounting rather than an oracle attack but no technical post-mortem names the exact flawed computation, hence low confidence on the precise mechanism.

violated_invariant: Pool shares minted by a single-asset join must be backed by a proportional token input; with the 8-decimal WBTC reserve compressed to dust, calcSingleInGivenPoolOut rounds the required input down to one satoshi while the full BPT is still minted, and joinswapPoolAmountOut has no minimum-effective-input or precision check.
notes: joinswapPoolAmountOut only requires tokenAmountIn != 0, <= maxAmountIn and <= MAX_IN_RATIO of the balance, so a 1-satoshi input for a large poolAmountOut passes once the reserve is dust; MIN_BALANCE is enforced only in bind/rebind. Slither raises nothing on this path; the reentrancy findings on joinPool/exitPool are marked invalid because both run under the _lock_ mutex.

violated_invariant: Share mint/redeem value must not depend on the pool's instantaneous slot0 price that a caller can move within the same transaction.
notes: Hypervisor.deposit prices shares with TickMath.getSqrtRatioAtTick(currentTick()) and getTotalAmounts(), both read from pool.slot0() with no TWAP or deviation check, and DepositProxy.properDepositRatio compares against the same spot-valued totals, so the gateway adds no protection. Slither only reports unused-return on the slot0 reads (true but not the oracle-trust weakness) and arbitrary-send-erc20 on the V3 callbacks, which are guarded by msg.sender == pool and are not the bug. Hypervisor B (0xc86b...) is a second victim with no prepared candidate.

violated_invariant: Only the SAFE owner (or an address it allowed) can move a SAFE's collateral; a shared library address must never be able to act as owner on behalf of arbitrary callers.
notes: GebProxyActions is a stateless DSProxy action library whose functions carry no authentication because they assume delegatecall; four SAFEs had the library address itself registered as ownsSAFE, so a direct call to quitSystem makes the manager see msg.sender == owner. The code weakness is the absence of a direct-call guard on the library; the registration itself was a user/integration error, so the label is medium-confidence and some reviewers may classify it as misuse rather than a defect. The arbitrary-send-eth findings on freeETH/exitETH describe the same direct-call hazard class but a different function and mechanism, so they are not counted as explaining.

violated_invariant: Free-collateral must correctly reflect a net fCash debt of any magnitude; an unbacked long position must never settle into withdrawable cash.
notes: ERC1155Trade.safeTransferFrom lets any caller mint a payer/receiver fCash pair from an account that holds nothing, and the payer's free-collateral check is the only backstop; ExchangeRate._convertToETH truncates the net balance with an unchecked uint128(balance.abs()) cast, so a ~2^128 debt wraps to a small value and the check passes. The receiver's unbacked claim then settles to cash and is withdrawn from Escrow. All five candidates are proxies whose Sourcify bundle includes the implementation source; the implementation addresses themselves are not candidates and no Slither detector covers unchecked narrowing casts.

violated_invariant: Each share class must be backed by assets accounted to that class only; one raw stETH balance must not back both rsvETH and rsvstETH, and only the owner may register new assets.
notes: The vault prices the rsvETH class off the diamond's raw stETH balance (getRemainingBalance returns balanceOf(vault)), and a permissionless registerErc20(stETH) lets an attacker deposit stETH under a second share class into that same balance, inflating rsvETH redemptions. Only the Diamond forwarding proxy source was recovered; the deposit/register facet is unverified and the InvestmentManagerFacet is not a candidate, so location names follow the PoC and selector matches rather than recovered source. Balancer (0xba12...) in the catalog row is the flash-loan source, not a victim.

violated_invariant: Collateral valuation must not be derived from a price the borrower can set by filling its own orders in the current block.
notes: getMarketUnitPrice returns blockTotalAmount*10000/blockTotalFutureValue for the current block once a small volume gate is met, so a flash-loan-funded cross-account self-trade at par pins the collateral price and lets a cheap lend position be withdrawn against as full collateral. Both candidates are EIP-1967 proxies and only the proxy source was recovered; the TokenVault/LendingMarketController implementations and OrderBookLib are not candidates, so locations come from the PoC's description of verified source rather than this bundle. The incorrect-return/incorrect-modifier findings are the standard transparent-proxy ifAdmin pattern.

violated_invariant: Only the buyer (or an address it authorized) may create an order that moves the buyer's account balance, and the seller written into an order must be validated.
notes: The factory entry (selector 0xbde886fc) checks only getState(buyer)==1, never msg.sender==buyer or a buyer signature, and accepts an attacker-supplied seller; it moves the buyer's whole Account System balance into a new order whose seller-gated abort() then sweeps it. All three contracts are unverified and no candidate has source or Slither output, so function names are the PoC's 4-byte-matched reconstructions and the root cause is inferred from the trace-based PoC only.

violated_invariant: Deposit shares must be minted on a valuation that cannot diverge materially from the market price of the deposited token.
notes: Shares are minted on the oracle-estimated value delta, and the FARM estimator reads a short-window Uniswap V3 TWAP from an imbalanced, thinly traded pool, so FARM bought cheaply on V2 is credited at roughly 9x and the inflated shares are redeemed for the strategy's UNI/AAVE/MKR. Mechanism is recorded as other because the PoC exploits a stale mispricing rather than manipulating the oracle pool itself. The strategy, controller and router proxies have no recovered source and the oracle is not a candidate, so the defect location name is the Enso oracle function the PoC describes, not recovered source.

violated_invariant: AtomicQueue may only pull want tokens from an address that chose to act as solver for this solve.
notes: solve() takes a caller-supplied solver and calls want.safeTransferFrom(solver, users[i], assetsToUser) with no check that solver is msg.sender or consented, so anyone with a standing want-allowance to the queue can be named as solver and drained up to a request the attacker wrote for itself. Slither's arbitrary-send-erc20 finding on that want transfer (index 1) describes exactly this; the offer-side instance (index 0) is the designed, request-gated flow. The catalog's 0x0000...4444 (V4 PoolManager) is only the cash-out venue.

violated_invariant: An ERC-20 transfer(to, amount) issued by a counterparty must move exactly `amount` token units; the same argument must not be reinterpreted as an NFT id that moves a full unit.
notes: O404.transfer treats any valueOrId <= maxTotalSupplyERC721 (50) as an NFT id and moves 1e18 units plus the NFT, so a Uniswap V3 exact-output swap for `id` wei makes the whitelisted pool pay out a full unit for ~2 wei of WETH; the pool is first made owner of low ids by repaying a V3 flash() via the id path. This is inherited ERC-404 design, but pairing it with a whitelisted AMM pool makes it exploitable, hence business_logic. The erc721-interface findings are correct about non-standard signatures but do not describe the dual interpretation.

violated_invariant: Borrow collateral must not be valued at a same-block spot price the borrower just moved, and a same-block guard must bind the actor (contract/position), not tx.origin.
notes: borrow() values deposited SPIRAL with poolManager.getSlot0() spot and lends ETH at LTV_BPS with no TWAP or deviation cap; the only defence, noSameBlockSwap, keys lastSwapBlockOf on tx.origin, so one pump tx followed by six borrows from fresh EOAs through the same attack contract clears the guard each time. Slither failed on the hook candidate (AssertionError, 0 findings), so there is nothing to adjudicate; the Spiral token candidate's findings are all library/informational and unrelated. Deployment block 25949176 is before the fork, so this is pre-patch code.

violated_invariant: Control of the Timelock (and therefore every gov-gated escape hatch such as masterFallback) must not be obtainable by a single ~3% token holder; quorumVotes/proposalThreshold are fixed absolute numbers with no participation floor, so with zero other voters one self-delegated stake clears both.
notes: Every contract behaved as written: the attacker bought ~504K YAM with real capital, self-delegated, and alone cleared the fixed quorum (2e29) and threshold on a dormant DAO, then took Timelock admin and used the gov-only masterFallback on both UMA farming contracts. Labeled governance_design rather than out-of-scope designed behavior because the taxonomy reserves that value for exactly this failure, but a reviewer could reasonably call it designed behavior, hence medium confidence. No Slither detector describes a low-quorum governance capture; the arbitrary-send/arbitrary-from findings are gated or governance-controlled and are false positives.

violated_invariant: Only an authorized caller may route a call through the Router to the Safe module; the Router's authorization check short-circuits to true when the multicall target is the Router itself, so a self-referential multicall runs the nested payload with the Router's own trusted identity.
notes: The defect is in the unverified private DeFi-Saver-style Router (0x4f00) whose multicall(address,bytes[]) trusts target==address(this); the enabled module (0xea18, also unverified) then forwards a DELEGATECALL recipe into the victim Safe. Neither defect contract has recovered source, so the location names come from the PoC/trace, not from Sourcify. The two candidates with source (GnosisSafeProxy, Aave aToken proxy) are forwarding proxies/dependencies, so no Slither finding is adjudicated and none explains the exploit.

violated_invariant: Vault share price must only reflect value the Strategy actually deposited; instead balanceOfY() values a Convex staked balance that anyone can inflate via permissionless stakeFor at the metapool's spot get_virtual_price, so a depositor can raise NAV between deposit and withdraw.
notes: The on-chain Strategy (0xb8d6) is a thin dispatcher: deposited() delegatecalls a governance-set impl (0xFf20DE3f, not among the candidates) that prices BaseRewardPool.balanceOf(Strategy) at spot virtual price; the NAV-inflation logic therefore lives partly outside the recovered source. Slither's controlled-delegatecall findings are false positives (fixed selector, impl set by governance) and no detector describes manipulable NAV accounting.

violated_invariant: initializeAccount must be callable at most once per account; the only guard is a transient-storage flag set in AccountProxy's constructor, which EIP-1153 keeps alive for the whole transaction, so anyone in the same tx can re-initialize a freshly deployed, pre-funded account with a malicious bootstrap.
notes: AccountProxy.sol and Initializable.sol (tstore/tload INIT_SLOT) are in the factory's recovered source and confirm the PoC; the account implementation 0x000000b8 that exposes initializeAccount is not a candidate, so that location is named from the PoC. Slither has no detector for transient-storage scoping, and its findings on the factory are generic (msg.value reachability, unused returns in OZ ERC1967Utils, benign reentrancy).

violated_invariant: UController.newOrganization must not register a caller-supplied avatar as a full-permission scheme over a Reputation contract that already belongs to another organization; it trusts the avatar's own nativeReputation() answer and never checks prior registration.
notes: The defect contract (shared UController 0xd5be) and the Avatar/Reputation/SchemeRegistrar are all unverified; only the unrelated DAOToken (GDT) has recovered source, so locations are named from the PoC's trace-decoded selectors. Attacker minted 20,000 REP against the real Reputation, voted itself in as a 0x1F scheme and drained 4.025 ETH. No Slither finding bears on the causal code.

violated_invariant: Total ETH paid back to a depositor (immediate bonus refund plus later withdraw) must not exceed the ETH deposited; deposit() both refunds the first-deposit bonus in ETH and adds the same bonus to the user's redeemable MUS allocation, with no cap.
notes: Sourcify has a partial match for MUSystem.sol even though the PoC calls the victim unverified; deposit() computes d.bonus, adds it to userTokenObtain and separately refunds amtToSend, which withdraw() never nets against. The attacker cycled fresh addresses with its own WETH (the PoC's flash loan is only working capital), so mechanism is 'other'. Slither's incorrect-equality on boolean compares and the arbitrary-send-eth on the owner fee transfer are false positives.

violated_invariant: A Safe module may only act for the Safe that actually enabled it, and may only call vetted routers; _start authenticates by asking msg.sender whether the module is enabled (self-attestation) and _swap does router.call(data) with caller-supplied router and data, so a fake Safe can make the adapter call execTransactionFromModule on real Safes that enabled it.
notes: Both flaws are confirmed in the verified adapter source (lines 92 and 189). Finding 1 (low-level-calls) points at the exact router.call(data) site but the detector only flags use of a low-level call, not an attacker-controlled target, so it is not counted as explaining. The Aave pool and Morpho candidates are infrastructure, not victims.

violated_invariant: Each unit of ETH received must be added to totalRewards exactly once; claimRewards adds (balance - lastETHBalance) on every call but only refreshes lastETHBalance when claimable > 0, so claimRewards([]) re-counts the same donation delta without bound.
notes: Verified source lines 1407-1432 match the PoC exactly. Slither flags claimRewards only for an uninitialized local (claimable, intentionally zero) and a low-level ETH send; neither describes the accounting asymmetry. The flash loan only supplied the ~27 ETH donation and was repaid.

violated_invariant: Expired buy-windows must settle at a manipulation-resistant price and only by an entitled party; accept() is open to anyone once expiry passes and _closeWindow/_buyBack use the same pool's instantaneous getSlot0 price with sqrtPriceLimit at MIN_SQRT_PRICE+1, so escrowed ETH can be mispositioned around a flash-moved spot and swept.
notes: All three facts (ungated accept after expiry at line 287, spot-price backInPlace test at 386, unbounded _buyBack limit at 443) are in the full-match source. Slither's 'timestamp' on accept() and 'unused-return' on getSlot0/swap touch the causal functions but describe different weaknesses, so explains is empty. The lib/v4-core findings (FullMath, BitMath, Hooks) are dependency code and were not adjudicated.

violated_invariant: Interest for an idle period must be accrued once at the utilization that prevailed during it; _checkFirstAction stores the whole 264,059-block gap and freezes actionEXR for the block, and the interest model then multiplies that full gap by a rate recomputed from live totals on every later action in the same block, so a flash-loan depositor sets the rate and collects ~36 days of interest repeatedly.
notes: The handler logic (TokenHandler, partial match) confirms _checkFirstAction; the interest model 0x29ec that applies the stored gap is not among the candidates, so that location is named from the PoC. UsdtHandlerProxy is a forwarding proxy and the affected market, not the defect. Slither's unused-return findings 70/85 sit on _checkFirstAction but only complain about ignored booleans, so they do not explain the exploit.
